text:
sara: quick heads up — ran a kernel-selection + batching sweep on TP 2x4 setup (8 GPUs) to investigate a perf regression we started seeing on medium-sized all-reduces. results look weird, posting notes below.

sara: command i ran:
```bash
NCCL_DEBUG=INFO ./bench/tp_allreduce --tp 2 --pp 4 --msg-sizes 4K,64K,256K,1M --batch-window=8 --kernel-mode=autoselect 
```

sara: summary: tiny msgs (<32KB) behave; large msgs (>512KB) stable; mid-range ~64KB-512KB shows 20-40% latency spike on ring path. tree fallback reduces tail by ~25%. KV-cache warmups shift distribution into the bad region. :thinking:

cheng: good reproduction steps, thanks. autoselect picks ring for our current kernel heuristics at those sizes? I thought we favored tree once msg > 128KB. maybe kernel scoring changed after the kernel-hotpatch last week.

mike: i repro'd on my local 8xA100 cluster. attach short perf snippet (trimmed):
```text
[256KB] allreduce: avg 68ms -> 210ms on ring path (bursty), tree: 160ms steady
cpu utilization drops during ring spikes, nvlink bw saturated for short windows
```

anita: @sara did you use the new batching heuristic (windowing) or the old continuous-batch? Those change effective message size (we pack 2-4 tensors into one all-reduce).

sara: yes windowing=8 (default of the new heuristic). that packs small tensors into mid-sized messages which moves more traffic into that 64-512KB band. i can re-run with window=1 (no coalescing).

infra-bot: perf-ci started 1934567905 for bench/tp_allreduce (id: perf-9932)

mike: try forcing NCCL to tree for mid sizes: set NCCL_ALGO=Tree for the run and compare. we might need a policy change: prefer tree when effective_msg > 64KB and kv_cache_hit_rate > 30%.

cheng: suggestion: kernel selection should consider measured interconnect utilization and not only msg size. ring overhead increases with more simultaneous streams. maybe our async-kernel scheduler is opening too many concurrent collectives during cache warmup.

sara: next steps I'm taking:
- re-run with --batch-window=1 and with/without KV cache enabled
- force NCCL_ALGO=Ring and NCCL_ALGO=Tree to get baseline
- dump nvprof/ncu traces for the 256KB spike window
- check kernel-scores from the autoselect codepath (logs enabled)

mike: if you can paste the autoselect log lines I can quickly see why it preferred ring. relatedly, we had a regression where kernel latency estimator forgot to include comm setup cost per-stream.

anita: also check the kvcache: if prefix hits push fewer tokens but more tensor merges, the per-step allreduce rate changes. worth measuring tokens->msg-size histogram.

sara: agreed. i'll post histograms and traces here. quick interim call: do we want to change default autoselect to bias tree for mid msgs until we fix estimator? vote? :eyes:

cheng: +1 to biasing tree temporarily. safer tail behavior.

mike: +1. also add a short-term metric in console: pct of allreduces using ring vs tree by msg-size bucket. make it visible in per-route dashboard.

anita: +1. and add a note to the rollout doc so Dedicated customers know about the temporary switch.

sara: i'll implement the temporary bias and rerun benches. posting results (and the ncu flamegraphs) once they are ready. thanks all. :thumbsup:
